articles.title: T. rex Was Warm Like You! Scientists Take a Dinosaur's Temperature
articles.summary: Scientists figured out how hot a T. rex was by testing its tooth! The giant dinosaur's body was about 97 degrees Fahrenheit — almost the same as a human's. That means T. rex was warm-blooded, not slow and cold like a lizard.

articles.title: Orcas Smash Sunfish Like a Piñata — and Scientists Are Stunned
articles.summary: In the Gulf of California, scientists filmed orcas ramming dead sunfish so hard the fish exploded into pieces. It might be a way to feed baby orcas — or just killer whale fun. One researcher said she was 'absolutely gobsmacked.'

articles.title: Cats Have a Secret 'ID Card' — Hidden in Their Pee!
articles.summary: Scientists found 13 special fatty acids in cat urine that work like a chemical ID card. Each cat's mix is different, and it lasts for hours. That's how cats know who left a scent mark — even months later.
